   Laura confirms eligibility and determines whether the Every.org route or direct coordination through Myriad USA is appropriate.

   Donors contribute through Every.org or through the direct route agreed with Myriad USA and receive the applicable U.S. tax receipt.

content:
# Receiving Funds from the U.S. > 1. Tax-deductible donations from individual donors > Step-by-step process
4. **Grant request to Myriad USA**\
   Before the funds are transferred, Laura submits OCE’s grant request in the Myriad USA portal. For each project, the request includes a short narrative describing the project and a project end date.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receiving Funds from the U.S. > 1. Tax-deductible donations from individual donors > Step-by-step process

content:

   Myriad USA transfers the approved funds to OCE as a grant.

content:

   Ivan allocates the funds to the intended collective on the Open Collective platform, with Michael overseeing financial control and reconciliation.

content:

Tier 1 applications are transferred to Ivan for contact, due diligence and onboarding. Laura retains Tier 2 and Tier 3 applications for direct contact and operational architecture. Ambiguous or high-risk applications are escalated to JF and, where relevant, Michael.

# Eligibility > Eligibility Criteria

**Be non-profit in nature**: Profits must not be distributed to members. For the types of contributions accepted through OSE, including the rules on membership benefits and other counterparty benefits, see [Contributions FAQ](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/contributions-faq/).

# Basics > Your first steps
1. **Check your public profile and contacts.** Use the platform's [Quick Start Guide](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/collectives/quick-start-guide). Keep administrator access and the main contact up to date, and notify OSE of changes.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Your first steps

content:
# Basics > Your first steps
2. **Choose how to receive funds.** Start with [donations and funding routes](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/). You can receive contributions without waiting for the optional welcome call.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Your first steps

content:
# Basics > Your first steps
3. **Agree how your Collective makes spending decisions.** Read [budget decisions](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/guides/deciding-on-how-to-use-your-money/).

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Your first steps

content:
# Basics > Your first steps
4. **Prepare your first payment.** Use [Pay and get reimbursed](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/); funds must be received and available before payment.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Your first steps

content:
# Basics > Your first steps
5. **Keep the community informed.** Use Updates and review the responsibilities below.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Your first steps

content:
# Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember
1. **Contracts and agreements**: Discuss and obtain acceptance before any arrangement requires OSE to sign a specific contract.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember

content:
# Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember
2. **Grant applications**: If OSE will be named as recipient or signatory, contact the team before submission so it can review and accept its role and commitments.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember

content:
# Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember
3. **Community updates**: Use the Updates feature to keep your community informed. Publish at least one update per year.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember

content:
# Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember
4. **Expenses**: Follow the [expense guide](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/expenses/) for documents, review and payment.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember

content:
# Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember
5. **Contributions**: OSE primarily supports donations and grants. Before committing to sales, invoiced services or contributions with promised benefits, contact OSE to discuss whether the arrangement can be supported and under what conditions. Do this before making commitments or receiving payment; acceptance is not guaranteed.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Top 5 Things to Remember

content:
# Basics > Important Notes
**Tax Obligations**: You’re responsible for understanding and fulfilling all of your tax obligations. If you’re not sure whether you need to charge or pay tax, we encourage you to consult a tax professional to better understand your tax obligations. OSE can’t provide tax advice.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Basics > Important Notes

# Applying for Grants > The grant journey
1. **Before submitting:** check the funder's requirements and contact OSE. If the application names OSE as recipient or signatory, OSE must review and accept that role before submission.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > The grant journey

content:
# Applying for Grants > The grant journey
2. **If awarded:** share the grant agreement and arrange the necessary agreements and payment instructions with OSE.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > The grant journey

content:
# Applying for Grants > The grant journey
3. **When funds arrive:** use the Collective budget in line with the funding conditions. A promised grant is not an available balance.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > The grant journey

content:
# Applying for Grants > The grant journey
4. **During the project:** prepare activity reports and project monitoring. OSE provides accounting information it holds and validates what engages OSE.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > The grant journey

content:
# Applying for Grants > Initial Steps
1. **Contact OSE early**

   Email <oce@opencollective.com> to let us know about the grant opportunity. We'll help assess whether it's compatible with fiscal hosting through OSE.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > Initial Steps

content:
# Applying for Grants > Initial Steps
2. **Check funder requirements**

   Not all funders allow grants to be awarded to fiscally sponsored initiatives. Be sure to confirm with them whether a hosted structure is accepted.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > Initial Steps

content:
# Applying for Grants > Initial Steps
3. **For U.S. funders**

   Contact the OSE team to arrange the documentation required by your funder. See [Equivalency Determination Certificate](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/equivalency-determination-certificate/).

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > Initial Steps

content:
# Applying for Grants > Grant Agreements & Receiving Funds
1. **Grant Agreement**

   The funder will provide a grant agreement. This must be signed by the confirmed recipient entity.\
   Please share the agreement with us via <oce@opencollective.com>, or have the funder reach out to us directly.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > Grant Agreements & Receiving Funds

content:

2. **Mandate Agreement**

   Your initiative will also need to sign a Mandate Agreement with OSE.\
   This formalizes the arrangement and must be signed by two members of your initiative.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > Grant Agreements & Receiving Funds

content:

3. **Bank Transfer**

   The OSE team will provide the appropriate bank transfer instructions for the agreed grant arrangement.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Applying for Grants > Grant Agreements & Receiving Funds

content:

   Once the grant is received, the funds will appear on your Collective’s Open Collective page as available balance.

**Common Concerns:**
Legal or tax implications: Open Source Europe cannot advise you on your members' or collaborators' legal or fiscal obligations. We recommend contacting a legal or fiscal specialist in their country of residence. For general guidance, please use this documentation or contact us at <oce@opencollective.com>

content:
# Deciding on How to Use Your Money > Decision-Making and Governance
**Common Concerns:**
Disagreements: Act in good faith and empower group decisions. Clear policies and consistent practices help a lot in this process.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Deciding on How to Use Your Money > Decision-Making and Governance

content:
# Deciding on How to Use Your Money > Decision-Making and Governance
**Common Concerns:**
*Intense up-front transparency*: invest in publishing details about the decisions transparently. Give contributors and spectators advance notice of possible expenditures, make it clear who has the power to decide, and offer a public comment period before approval. Do this consistently, and use Open Collective's tools to leave the records up for future inspection. This is relatively easy if you are managing all the expenses via Open Collective invoices.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Deciding on How to Use Your Money > Decision-Making and Governance

content:
# Deciding on How to Use Your Money > Decision-Making and Governance
**Common Concerns:**
*Post-decision accountability*: don't offer a pre-decision public comment period, but run an explicit private comment period among the decision markers, and offer accountability for past expenses such that anyone who wants to can ask for details on particular expenditure choices. This allows you to make more decisions privately, and gives you the option of providing some details privately in response to questions, but keep in mind that your payees or people you answer may publish details on their own.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Deciding on How to Use Your Money > Decision-Making and Governance

### How we work

Open Collective Europe is run by a small, multilingual, and fully remote team based primarily in Europe.\
We operate asynchronously across time zones, and value transparency, autonomy, and collaboration in our day-to-day work.

Our goal is to provide trusted and accessible infrastructure to communities and funders who share our vision for the commons.

## 1. Purpose of the role

JF leads Open Collective Europe’s strategy, organizational model and institutional development. He is responsible for ensuring that OCE has a clear direction, an economically sustainable operating model, appropriate governance and a team structure capable of delivering its mission.

JF is the final executive decision point for material strategic, contractual, financial, legal, reputational and resource matters within the authority delegated to him by the Foundation Board.

The Board retains its legal governance responsibilities and any decisions reserved to it. JF’s role is not to personally execute or recheck all operational work.

# Creation and Sending of Mandate Agreements

#### Purpose and scope

To ensure that mandate agreements are drafted, reviewed, signed, stored, and uploaded consistently and in line with OCEF requirements.\
This procedure applies to all mandate agreements.

#### **Introduction**

Mandate agreements define the relationship between OCE and the initiatives in cases where a formal document is needed to evidence the nature of the hosting arrangement to a third party, such as a grant maker. They clarify the respective roles and responsibilities of OCE and the hosted initiative in relation to a specific activity or arrangement. Mandate agreements are mandatory in cases involving the reception of a grant. Where a collective is only carrying out simple fundraising activities, the Terms of Hosting are sufficient and no mandate agreement is required.

#### Responsibilities

The Director initiates the process and indicates which template should be used.

Operations prepares the draft, performs the required checks, sends the agreement for signature, and ensures proper storage and upload.

Special cases may be identified and handled by either Operations or the Director, depending on the circumstances.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Creation and Sending of Mandate Agreements > Purpose and scope
metadata.heading_path: Creation and Sending of Mandate Agreements

# Receiving Funds from the U.S.

This page outlines how the Open Collective Europe Foundation (OCE) receives and processes funds from U.S.-based donors, including individual donors and private foundations.

OCE is not a U.S. legal entity, but we have structured mechanisms to legally and transparently receive U.S. funds.

{% hint style="danger" %}
**Important**: These services are available **only to collectives hosted by the Foundation,** not by the ASBL.

If a collective hosted under the ASBL wishes to access U.S. fundraising mechanisms, it must first be transferred to the Foundation. Contact the team to initiate this process.
{% endhint %}

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Receiving Funds from the U.S.
metadata.heading_path: Receiving Funds from the U.S.

### 1. Tax-deductible donations from individual donors

OCE works with **Every.org and Myriad USA** to allow eligible collectives hosted by the Foundation to receive tax-deductible donations from U.S.-based individuals and companies.

Every.org is generally used for public campaigns and repeated donations. Myriad USA acts as the U.S. fiscal sponsor, holds the donations and transfers the funds to OCE as a grant.

## Support Ops

This section introduces the internal operations and practices we follow to deliver high-quality support to hosted collectives, funders, and external stakeholders.

Open Collective Europe operates with a small team and a strong commitment to care, responsiveness, and legal compliance. Because we support a wide variety of collectives — many of which do not have formal structures — our support work often requires navigating nuanced legal, financial, and relational dynamics.

Support operations at OCE are not fully centralized: they rely on collaboration across roles (admin, ops, finance, and governance), and the ability to adapt to different funders, platforms, and jurisdictions.

This chapter includes:

**Access**:\ To get access to the canned response library, contact **Ivan**. You can also suggest new responses or edits if a situation comes up frequently.
After the onboarding call OCEFHi, Thank you for taking the time to speak with me earlier. I’d like to recap what we discussed about Open Collective Europe (OCE). OCE is a Belgian foundation for public benefit focused on supporting impactful initiatives. You can find our guidelines here and our technical documentation here. To summarise it, here are a few key points : Fundraising: OCE enables groups to raise money from various donors, including individuals, companies, and foundations. Grant Applications: Your group is eligible to apply for grants. If you're applying for a grant, please inform us in advance so we can coordinate with the grantor to provide the necessary information and sign the grant agreement. Responsibility: The collective's administrators are solely responsible for the collective's activities and management. Expense policy: This procedure applies for processing expenses. Bank Accounts: Your collective cannot have external bank accounts. All funds must be held in your Open Collective account to ensure an accurate representation of your budget and activities. Overhead costs: 8% for online (non-tax-deductible) donations. 10% for wire transfers, including grants from foundations and tax-deductible contributions from the US. Lastly, feel free to join our Discord community to stay connected, share your progress, and engage with the broader Open Collective community. Looking forward to seeing your initiative grow! Best regards,
Paypal fees for low funds Hi, Unfortunately your Collective does not have enough funds to cover for the fees of this payment method. Paypal reports its estimated PAYPAL fees on €XXXXXXX, but they are difficult to predict. If you wish to proceed with PayPal, you could either use the "payee is covering the fees solution" if possible or manually adapt the fees and use the "empty balance" feature (the procedure is described here https://docs.opencollective.com/help/collectives/collective-settings/zero-collective-balance). Otherwise, you can edit the payment method, select "New Bank Account" instead of "New Custom Payout Method" and write your coordinates in the form. After that, please make sure to re-approve the expense. Best regards,
Missing invoice Hi, Thank you for submitting your expense. To help us process this and get the funds to you as quickly as possible, we just need a small adjustment regarding the documentation. Following the Belgian regulations, we can only pay expenses which include a valid fiscal document (like a tax receipt or a tax invoice). While order confirmations are a great start, they unfortunately don't meet the legal requirements we must follow to protect the hosting infrastructure. Could you please upload the final receipt or invoice to your expense? It’s simple to update it: - Click on the edit icon. - Upload the document and save. Once you've updated it, don't forget that a collective admin will need to approve the expense. If you’re unsure where to find the right document or have any questions, feel free to check out our dedicated guide or just reply to this email. Best regards, [Your Name] Open Collective Europe
Apply through platform Hi, Thank you for applying to be fiscally hosted by Open Collective Europe. We would like to ask you to fill in the application form here https://opencollective.com/europe/apply to continue with the application procedure. For more information on the conditions, please check our documentation https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/ Also, please bear in mind that there is a minimum of two identifiable admins needed for a collective to be approved. If we don't hear from you within the next two weeks, we will not proceed with your application. Best regards, The OCE Team
Application rejection OSE Hi, Thank you for your application to be fiscally hosted by Open Source Europe, and for taking the time to share your project with us. After careful review, we have decided not to move forward with your application. Based on the information provided, we do not think the project is the right fit for OSE’s hosting framework at this stage. We appreciate your interest and wish you all the best with the development of your initiative. Best regards, The OSE Team
Change payment to New Bank Account Hi, In order to process this payment faster, would you please be able to edit the payment method, select "New Bank Account" instead of "New Custom Payout Method" and then write your coordinates in the form? Thank you for your help. Best regards,
Old Pending contribution - REGISTERED Hi, Thank you for your email - it helped us identify the contribution. It is now registered on the collective's page. Apologies for the delay, these are manual transactions and can slip under the radar sometimes in spite of our regular controls. Because of that we recommend to use the card payment/PayPal whenever possible. It automates the procedure, arrives instantly to the collective's page and has a bit lower fee. Best regards,
bank statement no Hi, In order for the expense to be paid, we kindly ask you to provide a valid fiscal document - a receipt or an invoice. The bank statement is not considered as such by the tax authority. Could you please attach it and re-approve the expense? For the general details on what the document should contain, please see our documentation here: https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/how-it-works/expenses Best regards,
Paypal multicurrency no Hi, would you please be able to submit the request in EUR and apply the today's exchange value? It is not possible for us to process multicurrency bills via Paypal. To edit the expense, select More actions>Edit> Thank you, Ivan
Apply through form Hi, Thank you for applying to Open Collective Europe. To continue with your application, please complete our form at https://www.oceurope.org/apply. This helps us better understand your collective and assess whether it’s a good fit for OCE. You can also review our documentation here for more details on the conditions: https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/ Please note that at least two identifiable admins are required for a collective to be approved. We look forward to your submission. Best regards, The OCE Team
Missing tax referenceHi, Thank you for submitting your expense! It appears that in the attached invoice a few required details are missing, so we’re not able to move forward with the payout just yet. To make sure the expense can be processed smoothly, could you please update the invoice to include the following information: A unique invoice number The full identification of the issuer (name, address, and tax or company registration number) A clear description of the service provided The applicable tax rate If the tax rate is 0%, please include a short note directly on the invoice explaining the reason (for example: VAT exemption under Article YY of Law XX). Please also note that the invoice should not mention Open Collective Europe You can update the invoice directly by clicking on the edit icon on the expense. Once edited, the expense will need to be approved again by a collective admin. If helpful, you can find more guidance on invoice requirements here: https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/how-it-works/expenses/invoices-or-reimbursements Thank you for your help. Best,
Closed for holidaysSeason greetings! Reduced service for the holidays We wanted to let you know in advance that we will be taking days off throughout the upcoming holiday season to spend some time on ourselves and with our families and friends. We won't be reimbursing expenses between 25 December and 2 January 2. To ensure your expense request is processed in time, please submit it by 21 December 2023 EoB. During this period, we may also take longer than usual to reply to your messages. If you have a query, feel free to check out our documentation, while we work through our support tickets. We’ll be back up to speed on 2 January taking care of any outstanding issues then. Happy holidays! The OCE Team
How to join OCEHow to join OCE To transfer your collective from OCF to OCE, please do the following: Spend down the balance in your OCF collective to $0. You can do this by paying out expenses or invoices or donating your remaining balance to another c3 organization. Unhost your collective from OCF (steps outlined here). Submit an application to be hosted by OCE here.
OCF TransitionThank you for reaching out and for your consideration. We appreciate your initiative and would be happy to host it. We believe you have already looked at this introduction, particularly our expenses guidelines. If you haven't, please let us know if they work for you. Regarding your collective's transition from OCF, please verify OCF's guidelines and contact them if you have any doubts or uncertainties about the obligations between your collective and their organization defined by their Terms and Conditions. If you have already decided to transfer your collective from OCF to OCE: You have to spend down the balance in your OCF collective to $0. You can do this by paying out expenses or invoices or requesting that your balance be moved to OCE (remember that this option might take time). Unhost your collective from OCF (steps outlined here). Submit an application to be hosted by OCE here. We would also welcome you if you decided to create a brand new collective and immediately start receiving donations. To do this, please read our documentation and apply to OCE here. Please respect the terms and conditions of the agreement you have in place with OCF, which does not allow one initiative to have two fiscal hosts (e.g., the new collective cannot be a duplicate of the old one). Feel free to reach out if you have specific questions. Our tech team is working on solutions to allow the collectives to export all their data and keep them after the dissolution of OCF. Here, you can find their latest update. We look forward to hearing from you. Best regards,
OOO GenericHi, Thank you for reaching out. I am currently out of the office and will not be able to respond to emails until [Date of Return]. During this time, I will have limited access to email. If your matter is urgent, please contact [Alternative Contact Person/Department] at [Alternative Contact Information]. For all other inquiries, I will respond to your email as soon as possible upon my return. Thank you for your understanding. Best regards, [Your Name]
Post check-in: add a second adminHi, we appreciate the latest update you posted and note that your collective is still active. We wish you all the best in continuing its activity and would like to ask you to add a second identifiable admin to your collective. It helps the transparency of your activity and ensures its continuity. It is also a mandatory requirement on OCE. Don't hesitate to reach out to us at oce@opencollective.Com if you have any questions or doubts. Kind regards, The OCE Team
Application rejection - no response to our questions OCEF Hi, Thank you for your application to be fiscally hosted by Open Collective Europe. We followed up a few weeks ago with some additional questions, but have not received a response. Since we need this information in order to continue reviewing your application, we will close your application for now. You are welcome to get back in touch at any time if you would like to resume the process. We wish you all the best with your project. Best regards, The OCE Team
KYC legal name Hi, Thank you for submitting the expense. To help us process this and get the funds to you as quickly as possible, we just need a small adjustment. Could you please enter your full legal name in the “Legal Name” section of your Profile settings? As the information in that section is not public, this will allow you to continue using your alias for public purposes while ensuring we meet our internal compliance requirements. In line with Belgian anti-money laundering (AML) regulations and our Know Your Customer (KYC) obligations, we are required to have the legal name of any individual receiving an expense payout. Thank you for your help and understanding. Best regards,
No news 2 weeks rejectionHi, We haven’t heard back from you after our last message, so we’ll assume you’ve decided not to move forward with the application for now. We wish you the best with your project, and if you ever decide to reapply in the future, you’re more than welcome to reach out. All the best, The OCE Team
No cryptoHi, Due to the strict AML requirements imposed by our banking providers and the Belgian tax authorities, OCEF cannot reimburse expenses where the primary documentation is denominated in cryptocurrency. It poses a serious risk of our bank accounts being flagged as "high risk", which may lead to their closing. For the time being, we can only pay out invoices and receipts denominated in fiat currency (EUR, USD, etc.), with complete tax information of the provider, to ensure fiscal traceability.
No reimbursement in a B2B exchangeHi, Thank you for submitting your request. Please note that it is unfortunately not possible to use the Collective’s funds to pay or reimburse expenses incurred by a registered company, such as a B2B invoice issued by one business to another. For this expense to be eligible, the invoice would need to be issued directly to the Collective. If you are acting on behalf of the business, you are welcome to issue a B2C invoice addressed to the Collective instead, including an individual admin's address, and VAT where applicable, and we’ll be happy to review it. For reference, please don’t hesitate to consult our guidelines here: https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/how-it-works/expenses. Please, let us know if you have any questions. Best regards,
PayPal verify / avoid Hi, Thank you for submitting the expense. We need just a small correction from your side to finish processing it. Due to recent changes in PayPal operations, processing payouts to PayPal accounts has become a completely manual task for us. This is why you may experience delays with this payment method. We strongly recommend providing a bank account number (IBAN) as a payout method instead for future expenses. This allows for automation and will greatly speed up the processing. If you still wish to be paid via PayPal, please verify your account. Thank you for your help. Best,
KYC create an organisation Hi, Thank you for submitting the invoice. As this appears to be an invoice from a registered business, could you please create an organization profile for the business, if you are its legal representative, and resubmit the invoice through that profile? Under Belgian AML and KYC regulations, we need to ensure that the profile holder matches the payee, especially for business payments. Here is how to do this: https://documentation.opencollective.com/getting-started/creating-an-organization Please include all of the business’s legal details in the organization profile. Thank you for your help! Best,
Business different than the account holderHi, Thank you for submitting the invoice. Everything looks good overall. We just need a small clarification: it is not clear to us what the relationship is between the business named on the invoice and the bank account holder. Could you please explain this for us, as we may need to clarify it with the tax office? Thank you for your help!
Grant request documentsHi, Thank you for submitting the grant request. To enable us to review and process it, could you please attach the following supporting documents: a copy of the organization’s legal bylaws (statuts) a signed letter formally requesting the grant, setting out: the purpose and objectives of the requested funding how the funds will be used in alignment with the fund’s mission the legal name and contact details of the nonprofit organization a bank account holder statement in the name of the nonprofit For more details, please see our guidelines here: https://docs.opencollective.com/oceurope/how-it-works/expenses/request-a-grant-for-nonprofits-only Thank you in advance. Best regards,
No fiscal deduction in the EUHi, thank you for your support. Unfortunately, individual donations in the EU are generally not fiscally deductible, as there is no single harmonized tax framework across EU countries. Tax rules vary by country, so we recommend checking what applies in your country of residence. Best regards,

# Financial Operations – Introduction

This section outlines the internal processes used by Open Collective Europe Foundation to manage financial operations across collectives, partners, and funders.

As a fiscal host, OCE is responsible for safely and transparently receiving, managing, and disbursing funds on behalf of more than 500 hosted initiatives.\
This documentation is intended for team members involved in financial workflows and compliance monitoring.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Financial Operations – Introduction
metadata.heading_path: Financial Operations – Introduction

content:
### Sections in this chapter

#### 1. Financial Ops Task Overview

A high-level summary of the recurring and ad hoc financial tasks handled by the team, including scheduling, responsibilities, and internal coordination.

#### 2. Bank Transfers for the Collective

Procedures for receiving and allocating manual bank transfers sent directly to OCE’s account. Includes how to match transfers to the correct collectives, and what to do when payment references are missing.

#### 3. Processing Expenses

How to handle submitted expenses: approval flow, supporting documents required, payout methods (Wise, PayPal), and timing expectations. Also includes how to handle edge cases (missing info, unusual currencies, etc.).

#### 4. Reconciliation Process

Step-by-step overview of how we reconcile platform data (Open Collective) with real bank activity. Covers matching transaction logs, resolving discrepancies, and updating internal records.

#### 5. Invoice and Corporate Donations

How to handle donations from companies that request invoices or proof of payment before contributing. This includes internal templates and who to loop in for confirmation and documentation.

#### 6. Refunds and Disputes

Covers cases where contributions need to be refunded, or where disputes arise (payment errors, double charges, fraud, etc.). Also includes the escalation process and coordination with OC Inc. or funders if needed.

#### 7. Budgeting and Forecasting

How we plan and track OCE’s internal budget. Includes tools used, funder projections, internal allocation of hosting fees, and how to support collectives in setting their own budgets.

#### 8. Platform Reconciliation with Bank Accounts

More technical procedures for reconciling the backend of the Open Collective platform with OCE's real bank accounts. Ensures our public-facing data matches accounting reality.

#### 9. Bank Accounts Management

Internal documentation on which bank accounts OCE uses, how access is managed, who initiates or approves transfers, and how Wise is integrated.

#### 10. Donations in Crypto Policy

How OCE handles cryptocurrency donations, via Every.org or other platforms. Covers which collectives are eligible, how crypto is converted, compliance concerns, and accounting treatment.

***

If you’re involved in OCE’s financial processes, this chapter is your reference.\
All new workflows or edge cases should be documented here to ensure traceability and consistency.

### Before Processing Payments

Before starting a payment batch, make sure that there are sufficient funds on the relevant Wise account of the host.

The Wise account of **OSE** receives contributions directly, so the budget is generally available.

The Wise accounts of **OCEF-EUR** and **OCEF-USD** must be recharged from:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Payment processing and disbursements > Before Processing Payments
metadata.heading_path: Payment processing and disbursements > Before Processing Payments

content:
Take transfer timing into account (plan ahead!) to avoid unnecessary delays; in particular with the USD transfers.

#### Recharging Wise EUR

To recharge **Wise EUR**:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Payment processing and disbursements > Recharging Wise EUR
metadata.heading_path: Payment processing and disbursements > Before Processing Payments

content: Amounts up to 20,000 EUR can be transferred from the KBC Projets Fondation - EUR account using the KBC Business Dashboard application. For amounts above 20,000 EUR, encode a wire transfer from the banking app. These transfers are immediate and free of charge. #### Recharging Wise USD The process for **Wise USD** is different. Transfers can **take up to a week to arrive** and incur bank charges on both the Wise and KBC sides. It is mandatory to go through the Add funds procedure on Wise, otherwise the arrival of the funds may be delayed or rejected. To recharge **Wise USD**:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Payment processing and disbursements > Recharging Wise USD
metadata.heading_path: Payment processing and disbursements > Before Processing Payments > Recharging Wise EUR

content: Wise charges **6.11 USD** regardless of the amount transferred. Add this amount to the total you are sending from KBC Brussels. For example, if you want that Wise receives exactly 50,000 USD, the wire amount from KBC should include the Wise fee: 50,000 USD + 6.11 USD = 50,006.11 USD The bank charges incurred on KBC Brussels for this transfer are in percentage, and are included in OCE operational costs through the monthly invoice issued by KBC Brussels. {% hint style="warning" %} USD transfers to Wise are not immediate. They can take up to a week and include charges. Plan USD liquidity in advance. {% endhint %}

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Payment processing and disbursements
metadata.heading_path: Payment processing and disbursements > Before Processing Payments > Recharging Wise USD

Payments are reviewed and processed **twice a week** (typically Tuesday and Thursday). This schedule may change depending on holidays, team availability, cash availability, urgent cases, or large payments that require direct processing from KBC. Most of the collectives are used to their disbursements being processed on Tuesdays.

**Open Collective** is the platform that OSE operates on. It provides tools for transparent budgeting, customizing a Collective profile, setting up tiers and goals, and more.

Please familiarize yourself with the guidelines on [donations](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/collectives/raising-money) and [expenses](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/submitting-expenses), and feel free to contact us if you have any questions or doubts at <oce@opencollective.com>.

Cryptocurrency is converted into conventional currency before it is allocated to the Collective. OSE does not pay cryptocurrency out to the Collective.

The Collective may ask OSE at any time to transfer the funds received on Every.org to its Open Collective budget. The team handles the intermediary steps. A request at any time does not mean an immediate payout; no fixed twice-yearly transfer schedule applies.

Can I refund a donation or get a refund for one I have made?

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Refunds

content:
## Can I request a refund for a donation?

Yes, under certain conditions. Open Source Europe (OSE) can process refunds for contributions made via credit card, bank transfer, or PayPal.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Refunds > Can I request a refund for a donation?
metadata.heading_path: Refunds > Can I request a refund for a donation?

content:
> **Important**: Refunds are only issued to the original payment method. For card payments processed through Stripe, Stripe and the card issuer handle the routing of the refund, including where the original card has expired or been replaced. OSE reviews the request and initiates an approved refund; it does not control the bank's handling of the funds.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Refunds
metadata.heading_path: Refunds > Can I request a refund for a donation? > Refund Timeframes

content:
## How to Request a Refund

Contact the Collective administrators first; they forward your request to OSE. If the administrators do not respond, contact OSE directly at <oce@opencollective.com>. A request does not guarantee a refund. Include the following details:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Refunds > How to Request a Refund
metadata.heading_path: Refunds > How to Request a Refund

content:
> **Note**: After reviewing the request, OSE may decline a refund if the contribution was authorized and the funds have already been used to support the Collective's activities.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Refunds
metadata.heading_path: Refunds > How to Request a Refund

content:
## Refund Processing Times

OSE first reviews the refund request. If approved, OSE initiates the refund. The time it takes for the funds to reach you then depends on the payment method, payment provider and bank. No fixed processing or receipt date is guaranteed.

These processing steps are separate from the request deadlines above: 90 days for card or bank-transfer contributions and 60 days for PayPal.

***

metadata.heading_path: Refunds > Refund Processing Times

**Ready?** Go to [Submission Process](#submission-process). **Already submitted?** Read [Approval Workflow](#approval-workflow), or use the expense comments for routine follow-up. Send sensitive information privately.

content:
## Overview

Managing expenses with Open Source Europe (OSE) is designed to be transparent and straightforward. Whether you're reimbursing a team member or paying a service provider, the process ensures accountability and compliance with fiscal regulations.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > Overview
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Overview

content:
## Before spending and requesting reimbursement

OSE does not require systematic advance approval for ordinary expenses. If eligibility is unclear, contact the team before spending. Reimbursement remains subject to review. Any arrangement requiring a specific contract signed by OSE must be discussed and accepted in advance.

If someone cannot advance the cost, direct payment to the supplier on a compliant invoice is possible. OSE does not provide advances to individuals.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > Before spending and requesting reimbursement
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Before spending and requesting reimbursement

content:
## Types of Expenses

There are two primary types of expenses you can submit:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > Types of Expenses
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Types of Expenses

content:
### 1. **Reimbursements**

Used when someone has paid out-of-pocket for goods or services on behalf of the Collective.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > 1. **Reimbursements**
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Types of Expenses > 1. **Reimbursements**

content: > **Note**: Order confirmations, proforma invoices, or bank statements are not valid receipts. Learn more: [How to Submit a Reimbursement](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/reimbursement)

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Types of Expenses > 1. **Reimbursements**

content:
### 2. **Invoices**

Used when paying individuals or organizations for services rendered.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > 2. **Invoices**
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Types of Expenses > 2. **Invoices**

content:
> **Important**: Invoices must be addressed to the Collective or the person who placed the order. OSE acts only as the payer for these purchases. Collectives must not use OSE’s legal name or VAT number to have invoices issued. Learn more: [How to Submit an Invoice](https://docs.opencollective.com/help/expenses-and-getting-paid/invoices)

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Types of Expenses > 2. **Invoices**

content:
## Supporting documents and timing of submission

Without an invoice or receipt, OSE refuses reimbursement; a bank statement alone is insufficient. For durable equipment, the usual supporting documents are required; OSE does not systematically require an additional inventory. Specific funding or agreement requirements still apply.

There is no general fixed deadline for submitting a reimbursement, but deadlines attached to a funding agreement or closure must be respected. Expenses incurred before the Collective was accepted by OSE may be reimbursed after review of their connection to the project, documents and funding conditions, provided funds are available.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > Supporting documents and timing of submission
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Supporting documents and timing of submission

content:
## Paying service providers

Collectives can pay service providers against a compliant invoice, including through a workers’ cooperative. Agree the work, price and dates with the Collective and submit the invoice through Open Collective for review. OSE does not provide a standard employment or payroll service. Any arrangement requiring OSE to sign a specific contract must be discussed and accepted beforehand.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > Paying service providers
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Paying service providers

content:
> **Processing Time**: We aim to initiate payment within seven business days once the expense is complete and approved and the necessary funds have been received and are available. Bank processing time is additional. This is a target, not a guaranteed date of receipt.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Submission Process

content:
## Approval Workflow

Expenses are reviewed by the Collective and OSE. If the sole administrator requests their own reimbursement, OSE can check the supporting documents and pay without a second approver on the Collective side.

OSE checks the documents before payment. Incomplete or non-compliant expenses may be rejected. A promised donation or grant is not an available balance: funds must be received and available before payment.

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > Approval Workflow
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Approval Workflow

content:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Expenses > Payment Methods
metadata.heading_path: Expenses > Payment Methods

content:

content:
## General Principles

Collectives hosted by Open Collective Europe (OCE) are unincorporated initiatives primarily funded through donations. As such, they are **not eligible for VAT refunds** and must **always pay VAT** on goods and services purchased.

VAT (Value Added Tax) is a general consumption tax that applies to most goods and services within the European Union. Even if your Collective is not a registered entity, VAT is still due on your expenses.

> **Note:** Learn more: [VAT explained – European Commission](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/vat_en)

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: VAT in Europe and How It Works in OCE > General Principles
metadata.heading_path: VAT in Europe and How It Works in OCE > General Principles

content:
## VAT Within the Same Country

Invoices issued within your country (e.g. Belgium) must include VAT unless the supplier is legally exempt.

OCE itself is **not VAT-exempt**, so if it issues an invoice (e.g. for services), VAT will be applied based on the applicable Belgian rate.

> **Note:** Belgian VAT details: [Finance Belgium](https://finance.belgium.be/en)

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: VAT in Europe and How It Works in OCE > VAT Within the Same Country
metadata.heading_path: VAT in Europe and How It Works in OCE > VAT Within the Same Country

content:
## Cross-Border VAT and Reverse Charge

The **reverse charge mechanism** lets VAT-registered businesses handle cross-border VAT internally (by declaring both output and input VAT).

However, this mechanism **only applies between two VAT-registered businesses**. Because OCE-hosted Collectives are **not legal entities**, they cannot apply the reverse charge mechanism.

> **Danger:** This means you **must pay VAT** on cross-border invoices from EU-based suppliers — just like any individual or unregistered group.

> **Note:** Learn more: [EU VAT rules – Your Europe](https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/taxation/vat/vat-rules-rates/index_en.htm)

***

metadata.breadcrumb_path: VAT in Europe and How It Works in OCE > Cross-Border VAT and Reverse Charge
metadata.heading_path: VAT in Europe and How It Works in OCE > Cross-Border VAT and Reverse Charge

# Deciding on How to Use Your Money

How to use funds for your initiative on OSE

This guide is based on an Open Source Collective workshop led by Sumana Harihareswara of Changeset Consulting in January 2022. It focused on helping Open Collective-hosted open-source software projects decide how to use the money they have already raised. We adapted it for user cases seen on OSE, with all examples in EUR.

content:
## Driver and Supporter/Protector Activities

**Drivers:** Activities that directly advance your mission (e.g., software development).

**Supporters:** Infrastructural activities and purchases that support drivers (e.g., organising conferences, buying laptops).

**Protectors:** Activities or expenses that reduce risks (e.g., legal fees, code of conduct workshops).

For instance, in this diagram...

[Image: Diagram of money and resources flowing into a project from creators, individual users, platforms and organisational users, and out to platforms and services, labour, convenings and travel, equipment and supplies, and outgoing donations and grants]

*Money and Resources, shown by those that go into a project and then what comes out of it*

...labor for software development is a driver, because writing the software directly advances the mission of making and improving the open source project. An example of a supporter activity: organizing a conference where the contributors can meet to improve and speed up their work. An example of a supporter purchase: buying a new laptop for a contributor to use.

content:
## **I sent in money but I don't see my donation on the collective's page?!**

[Contact us!](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/about/contact-us/)

We often receive money in our bank account without any indication of where it should go. (This is why it's so important to include the order# in the bank transfer). We always do a thorough research to identify the right collective, but sometimes it is not possible.

At the end of the month, we move the unidentified funds to a [holding fund](https://opencollective.com/oce-holding-fund).

We keep the money there until we can identify who it is intended for and then we transfer it.

Write to us on <oce@opencollective.com> or send us a message via[ Slack](http://slack.opencollective.com/) or [Discord](https://discord.gg/uCnzytpNr6). We will ask you to send us screenshots/receipts that include the expected amount, the collective name, and the sender/any info about the bank transfer, so that we can send the funds to their happy home.

Do this before making commitments or receiving payment; acceptance is not guaranteed.

Open Collective already includes crowdfunding tools and is the usual option. External platforms such as Patreon, Ko-fi or GoFundMe are considered case by case. The team checks payout arrangements, supporting records and any promised benefits; compatibility and acceptance are not automatic.

# Mission, Vision & Impact areas

It all comes back to resilience

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas
metadata.heading_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas

content:
## Mission

Open Collective Europe has set out to achieve the sustainability of the social and solidarity economy as well as open source technologies. Our mission is to enable initiatives to raise and spend money transparently under a common umbrella nonprofit.

*Open Collective is not a typical company. It is an ecosystem where a software company coexists with independent associations and foundations that we call 'hosts.' Open Collective Europe is blossoming as one of the first major fiscal hosts on the European continent. We host initiatives that share our values and work towards a better future. But what are those values? Our vision for a healthy and thriving world starts with resilience. Out of that central concern, we find six related areas where we want to make a difference.*

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Mission
metadata.heading_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Mission

content:
### Resilient communities

Humanity is divided on countless fronts, but most will agree on the need for resilience. When systems fail, we need fallback buffers. Resilient communities don't break due to cascading system failure. They have a patchwork of fallbacks to absorb the shocks. Resilience is when people next to you on the street know how to administer CPR or can swim to save someone from drowning. It is when the families in your neighborhood own their own homes. It is when your community has enough nurses to deliver your children and enough teachers to educate them. It is when every other house in your neighborhood has solar panels, feeding spare capacity back to the grid. It is when authorities arrive at a natural disaster and find that the local community has already started helping itself. It is a society of ordinary people who are great leaders when they need to be. Resilience keeps people, jobs, and services in your hometown. And when we can trust our community to catch us if we fall, we can safely turn our attention to working for the greater good. That is why we put resilient communities at the center of our mission.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Resilient communities
metadata.heading_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Mission > Resilient communities

content:
### Open innovation

When we use science and technology wisely, it makes us more resourceful. We expand our horizons and capabilities. If we share our findings, we grow stronger together. We foster collaboration and accelerate the dissemination of knowledge and technology through the network effect. Otherwise, we risk becoming divided by increasing technological gaps. Civil society plays a vital role in making innovation available to all. Distributed networks of passionate people around the world develop open-source software. Citizen scientists collect and share data. Civil engineers document how to build more energy-efficient homes. Technologists share blueprints for 3D printers and robots. Maker spaces around the world help people innovate and repair. What makes all of this possible is open innovation.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Open innovation
metadata.heading_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Mission > Open innovation

content:
### Commons stewardship

When a social innovation, cultural institution, or green space starts feeling like it has always been there, it has become a common good. We hope the commons we create will become so readily available that they appear unremarkable. And it is precisely at this point that it becomes vulnerable. Humankind longs for innovation, novelty, and excitement. We want to solve the urgent problems of the day, and that is where we focus our attention. But we also need to pay attention to maintaining the solutions to problems we have already solved. Once saved from deforestation, a forest needs protection from invasive species. A community center built by one generation must be repaired and maintained by the next. Technology that encrypts websites and emails and keeps us safe from surveillance must be updated. We cannot take our commons for granted. If we do, all our work on communities, solidarity, culture, innovation, and ecologies risks being undone. We need to support commons stewardship for our progress to leave a lasting legacy.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Commons stewardship
metadata.heading_path: Mission, Vision & Impact areas > Mission > Commons stewardship

We are based in Europe but offer fiscal hosting to initiatives around the world. If our vision speaks to you, get in touch. We are ready to host your collective today and would be excited to hear from you. [You can apply here.](https://www.oceurope.org/apply)

## Collective Infrastructure

As an umbrella organisation, OSE acts as the fiscal host for over 400 initiatives. Each project operates independently on the Open Collective platform with its own public page and transparent budget, while benefiting from the legal standing of a professional Belgian non-profit (ASBL/vzw).

This structure allows communities to manage funds, pay service providers on compliant invoices, and receive grants without the overhead of maintaining their own legal entity.

> **Tip:** ## Responsibilities and Alignment
>
> To maintain the integrity of the umbrella, hosted projects must adhere to three core principles:
>
> 1. **Mission Alignment:** Projects must actively support the development or sustainability of open source software.
> 2. **Non-Profit Compliance:** As an ASBL/vzw, projects must operate within the limits of Belgian law, focusing on community benefit rather than purely commercial for-profit activities.
> 3. **Operational Transparency:** All financial activities must be conducted through the Open Collective platform to ensure public accountability.

## Grants from U.S. foundations

Open Source Europe helps hosted projects receive grants from U.S. foundations through an Equivalency Determination (ED) arrangement.

Contact the OSE team before applying. We coordinate with the funder, provide the relevant documentation and arrange for the grant to reach your project.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Grants from U.S. foundations
metadata.heading_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Grants from U.S. foundations

content:
## Preparing a grant application

Contact <oce@opencollective.com> early, with:

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Preparing a grant application
metadata.heading_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Preparing a grant application

content: The team will provide the current ED documentation and confirm the details to use in the grant agreement. An ED does not guarantee that a particular funder or grant programme will accept an application.

metadata.heading_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Preparing a grant application

content:
## Donations from individuals

An ED is distinct from the route for U.S. tax-deductible donations through Myriad USA. See [Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/tax-deductible-giving-for-us-donors/).

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Donations from individuals
metadata.heading_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Donations from individuals

content:
## Documentation for the funder

The ED used for this arrangement is held by Open Collective Europe Foundation. Where this route is used, it receives the grant and transfers it to OSE for your project. The OSE team coordinates these steps.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Documentation for the funder
metadata.heading_path: Equivalency Determination Certificate > Documentation for the funder

content:
## An established route for U.S. giving

U.S. individuals and businesses can support OSE Collectives through **Myriad USA → Open Collective Europe Foundation (OCEF) → OSE**. This established arrangement enables U.S. tax-deductible donations within the limits of applicable tax rules. The donor’s actual deduction depends on their circumstances.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors > An established route for U.S. giving
metadata.heading_path: Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors > An established route for U.S. giving

content:
## Choose the appropriate donation route

Contact OSE at <oce@opencollective.com> before payment with the name of the Collective to support. The team organises the route, reference, documents, applicable costs and transfer arrangements.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors > Choose the appropriate donation route
metadata.heading_path: Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors > Choose the appropriate donation route

content:
A donation through the ordinary Open Collective checkout does not automatically use this arrangement. Confirm which organisation will issue the donation documentation for the selected route.

The [current OSE hosting fees](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/general-faqs/#how-much-does-it-cost) apply. The team will confirm any additional costs associated with the route.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors
metadata.heading_path: Tax-Deductible Giving for U.S. Donors > Choose the appropriate donation route

content:
## Other cases

If the tax-deductible route for your circumstances has not already been confirmed, contact OSE before giving to check the available route and documents. OSE does not guarantee an individual tax benefit.

Cryptocurrency donations have a specific mandatory Every.org starting point: see [Cryptocurrency contributions](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/how-it-works/financial-contributions-how-to-donate/contributions-in-cryptocurrencies/).

For grants from U.S. foundations, see [Equivalency Determination Certificate](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/what-we-offer/equivalency-determination-certificate/).

Further information: [Myriad FAQ](https://myriadusa.org/about/faqs/) and [ways to give](https://myriadusa.org/waystogive/).

# About Open Source Europe

Open Source Europe is a Belgian Association that fiscally hosts over 400 initiatives and partners with philanthropic institutions to support global regranting.

***

metadata.heading_path: About Open Source Europe

## Service Overview

Unlike traditional non-profits, Open Source Europe (OSE) combines a legal structure with a dedicated digital infrastructure to enable:

metadata.heading_path: About Open Source Europe > Service Overview

content:
## How hosting works

OSE provides a Belgian nonprofit home for open source projects. We use the Open Collective platform to manage budgets, receive contributions and process expenses transparently.

See our [Terms of Service](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/terms-of-service/) for the hosting agreement.

***

metadata.heading_path: About Open Source Europe > How hosting works

content:

[Contact the team](mailto:oce@opencollective.com)

***

metadata.heading_path: About Open Source Europe > How to Work With Us

content:
## A little history

Open Source Europe grew out of Open Collective Europe's fiscal hosting work. As that work developed, OSE became the home for open source projects and communities, while Open Collective Europe Foundation developed its wider philanthropic activities. Our hosting agreement still uses the association's name, Open Collective Europe ASBL/vzw.

Today, OSE focuses on helping open source communities receive funding, pay contributors and manage their projects transparently.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: About Open Source Europe > A little history
metadata.heading_path: About Open Source Europe > A little history

content:
## Hosting agreement

Hosting with Open Source Europe is governed by the association's Terms of Hosting.

The [Terms of Hosting for the association](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15Wkvfn5ou-is_eUjautjDv4JZ-tiY2-c/edit) are the reference document for this hosting relationship. [Contact the team](mailto:oce@opencollective.com) to obtain the applicable version and any additional agreement relevant to your project.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Terms of Service > Hosting agreement
metadata.heading_path: Terms of Service > Hosting agreement

content:
## Main responsibilities

This overview explains the main points of the association's Terms of Hosting. It does not replace or amend the agreement.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Terms of Service > Main responsibilities
metadata.heading_path: Terms of Service > Main responsibilities

content:
## Starting, changing or ending the arrangement

Contact the team before entering into grant agreements, making commitments on behalf of the association, or changing your project's activities.

The Terms of Hosting provide for termination with **30 days' written notice**. Valid outstanding expenses and any remaining balance are handled under the agreement's termination provisions. A remaining balance is not automatically available for distribution to individual administrators.

For current guidance on contributions, see [Contributions FAQ](https://opensourceeurope.org/docs/faq/contributions-faq/). If your planned activity raises a question about the scope of the hosting agreement, contact the team before proceeding.

metadata.breadcrumb_path: Terms of Service > Starting, changing or ending the arrangement
